extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in political economy, monetary policy, and fiscal/banking regulation
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive principles and evaluative distinctions from Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations on banking, paper money, and the accumulation of capital (productive vs unproductive labour). Includes policy prescriptions, classifications, and causal claims about capital, revenue, and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum denomination of bank notes
rubrics_metrics.description: It were better, perhaps, that no bank notes were issued in any part of the kingdom for a smaller sum than £5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smith argues smaller-denomination notes cause inconvenience to poor people and wider circulation of small notes displaces gold and silver from general circulation; cites London practice of no bank notes under £10 and suggests £5 outside London as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confine paper money to dealer-to-dealer circulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper money would then, probably, confine itself, in every part of the kingdom, to the circulation between the different dealers, as much as it does at present in London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When paper is mainly used between dealers (not consumers), gold and silver remain plentiful. Extending paper to dealer-consumer circulation (as in Scotland or North America) banishes coin from ordinary transactions. Policy implication: limit paper's role to wholesale/dealer circulation to preserve specie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banks may assist industry without extensive small-note issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Though no paper money, therefore, was allowed to be issued, but for such sums as would confine it pretty much to the circulation between dealers and dealers; yet partly by discounting real bills of exchange, and partly by lending upon cash-accounts, banks and bankers might still be able to relieve the greater part of those dealers from the necessity of keeping any considerable part of their stock by them unemployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable banking functions (discounting bills, lending against cash-accounts) allow banks to support commerce even if small circulating notes are restricted; policy can restrict notes but leave other banking operations free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for legal restraints on banking liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: Those exertions of the natural liberty of a few individuals, which might endanger the security of the whole society, are, and ought to be, restrained by the laws of all governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy given: obligation to build party walls to prevent fire is similar in kind to banking regulations. Regulation is legitimate when individual freedom threatens collective security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable paper money equals specie if payable on demand by credible issuers
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper money, consisting in bank notes, issued by people of undoubted credit, payable upon demand, without any condition, and, in fact, always readily paid as soon as presented, is, in every respect, equal in value to gold and silver money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key attributes: issuer credibility, unconditional immediate payment, practical redeemability. Such paper circulates at parity because gold/silver can always be had for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional or deferred promissory notes degrade in value
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper money, consisting in promissory notes, of which the immediate payment depended ... upon a condition ... or of which the payment was not exigible till after a certain number of years, and which, in the mean time, bore no interest ... would, no doubt, fall more or less below the value of gold and silver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment depends on issuer's will, on holder's fulfilling a condition, or is long-dated and non-interest bearing, the paper will trade at discount relative to specie; such features undermine currency value and exchange parity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of optional deferred-payment clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: The same act of parliament which suppressed ten and five shilling bank notes, suppressed likewise this optional clause, and thereby restored the exchange between England and Scotland to its natural rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional clauses that permit banks to defer payment (e.g., six months at directors' option) create uncertainty and discount; legislative suppression of such clauses corrects exchange distortions (example: Scotland 1762–1764).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clauses requiring change for small payments degrade notes and should be unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: In the paper currencies of Yorkshire, the payment of so small a sum as 6d. sometimes depended upon the condition, that the holder of the note should bring the change of a guinea to the person who issued it ... An act of parliament, accordingly, declared all such clauses unlawful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any conditional requirement that makes small-note redemption practically difficult (e.g., holder must bring large change) degrades currency; law can and should declare such clauses unlawful to protect holders and currency value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government long-term paper as legal tender is unjust and devaluing
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper currencies of North America consisted ... in a government paper, of which the payment was not exigible till several years after it was issued ... To oblige a creditor, therefore, to accept of this as full payment for a debt of £100, actually paid down in ready money, was an act of such violent injustice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonial government-issued long-dated paper declared legal tender forces creditors to accept far-discounted instruments; Smith condemns this as fraudulent and unjust. He praises parliamentary acts that forbid future emissions being legal tender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-acceptability can give paper additional value
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper of each colony being received in the payment of the provincial taxes ... it necessarily derived from this use some additional value, over and above what it would have had, from the real or supposed distance of the term of its final discharge and redemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When government accepts its paper for taxes, demand increases and the paper may trade closer to face value; extent depends on how much paper is issued relative to tax needs. Limited issuance relative to tax liabilities can even create a premium (agio).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank-money agio explanation is questionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Some people account in this manner for what is called the agio of the bank of Amsterdam ... This account of the bank of Amsterdam, however, it will appear hereafter, is in a great measure chimerical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smith notes explanations that ascribe bank-money premiums to careful limitation of bank-money supply may be illusory; he signals further analysis later. Caveat: apparent premiums have other causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper currency depreciation does not determine metal-to-goods ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper currency which falls below the value of gold and silver coin, does not thereby sink the value of those metals ... The proportion between the value of gold and silver and that of goods ... depends ... upon the richness or poverty of the mines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes currency-specific depreciation from fundamental value relations between metals and goods, which depend on supply and labour required to bring metals to market, not on a particular paper issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict small-denomination circulating notes and require unconditional redemption
rubrics_metrics.description: If bankers are restrained from issuing any circulating bank notes, or notes payable to the bearer, for less than a certain sum; and if they are subjected to the obligation of an immediate and unconditional payment of such bank notes as soon as presented, their trade may, with safety to the public, be rendered in all other respects perfectly free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy package: (1) set a legal minimum denomination for bearer/circulating notes, (2) require immediate, unconditional redemption on demand — then permit free banking otherwise to operate safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplication and competition among banks increases public security
rubrics_metrics.description: The late multiplication of banking companies ... instead of diminishing, increases the security of the public. It obliges all of them to be more circumspect ... divides the whole circulation into a greater number of parts ... By dividing the whole circulation into a greater number of parts, the failure of any one company ... becomes of less consequence to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competition constrains risky expansion of currency, reduces systemic impact of any single failure, and encourages banks to be liberal to customers to retain business; supports freer entry into banking under the constraint of denomination/redemption rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: productive vs unproductive labour
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one sort of labour which adds to the value of the subject upon which it is bestowed; there is another which has no such effect. The former ... may be called productive, the latter, unproductive labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Productive labour fixes value in a vendible commodity (e.g., a manufacturer). Unproductive labour (e.g., menial servants, many public officers, actors, musicians) does not fix value in durable commodities though it has value and deserves reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for productive labour: realization in vendible commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: The labour of the manufacturer fixes and realizes itself in some particular subject or vendible commodity, which lasts for some time at least after that labour is past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If labour results in a commodity that endures (even briefly) and can later set in motion equivalent labour, it is productive. Wages advanced to a manufacturer are restored with profit in the improved value of the subject worked upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of many public/professional services as unproductive
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign, for example, with all the officers both of justice and war who serve under him, the whole army and navy, are unproductive labourers ... In the same class must be ranked ... churchmen, lawyers, physicians, men of letters of all kinds; players, buffoons, musicians, opera-singers, opera-dancers, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although useful, honourable, or necessary, these services produce nothing that can afterwards purchase an equal quantity of labour; their output 'perishes' at the moment of production. This is a classification for analyzing capital and revenue, not a moral condemnation of workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual produce divides into replacement of capital and revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: When [produce] first comes ... it naturally divides itself into two parts. One of them ... is destined for replacing a capital, or for renewing the provisions, materials, and finished work ... the other for constituting a revenue either to the owner of this capital ... or to some other person, as the rent of his land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement-of-capital funds maintain productive hands only; revenue funds may maintain productive or unproductive hands. This accounting distinction determines long-run productive capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital vs revenue use determines who is maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: That part of the annual produce ... which replaces a capital, never is immediately employed to maintain any but productive hands. That which is immediately destined for constituting a revenue ... may maintain indifferently either productive or unproductive hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and social outcomes hinge on how produce is allocated: diverting capital-replacement to immediate consumption or to unproductive maintenance reduces future productive capacity and aggregate wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parsimony as immediate cause of capital accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitals are increased by parsimony, and diminished by prodigality and misconduct. Whatever a person saves from his revenue he adds to his capital ... Parsimony, and not industry, is the immediate cause of the increase of capital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry produces the goods that can be accumulated, but saving (parsimony) is what actually increases capital. Thus policies fostering saving/capital formation encourage greater future productive capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion of capital to revenue determines industry vs idleness
rubrics_metrics.description: The proportion between capital and revenue, therefore, seems everywhere to regulate the proportion between industry and idleness. Wherever capital predominates, industry prevails; wherever revenue, idleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In places where revenue (spending) predominates (courts, cities with large stationary revenues), there tends to be more idleness; where capital employment predominates (trade/manufacture), there is more industry. Changes in capital availability thus shape social character and economic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saved funds are consumed by different people than spent revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: What is annually saved, is as regularly consumed as what is annually spent, and nearly in the same time too: but it is consumed by a different set of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings typically feed productive hands (capital employment) while current expenditures of revenue feed unproductive dependents (servants, idle classes). Thus distributional effects of saving vs spending matter for productive capacity.
